To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) MOEA/D is very sensitive to its component-level configuration, and (ii) this is especially true when using a limited number of function evaluations.

the convergence of a decomposition-based MOEA on a limited budget is affected by choice: (1) whether information is shared between neighbouring subproblems; and (2) whether the normalisation scheme used in the decomposition is appropriate.

(1) the convergence of the MOEA/D algorithm, on a limited budget, varies significantly with the component-level configuration of the algorithm, and (2) the convergence of MOEA/D, on a limited evaluation-budget, is highly sensitive to the normalisation scheme that is used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practical question of how to configure MOEA/D for limited budgets, and provides a number of insights that can help practitioners to achieve better convergence in this setting.
the question: how can a decomposition-based optimizer be configured to provide good convergence on a limited number of evaluations?
the question of what is the most important configuration setting for MOEA/D on a limited budget, and how should it be configured to obtain the best convergence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MOEA/D with a normalisation scheme based on the maximum objective value, and no sharing, is the best option for a limited evaluation budget.
, in terms of performance, there is no single best configuration of MOEA/D for a limited budget.
MOEA/D with a normalisation scheme based on a reference point that is not the origin is a promising choice of algorithm on a small budget for problems with a convex Pareto front.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the choice of component-level settings can have a significant effect on the convergence of a multi-objective decomposition-based algorithm on a limited evaluation budged, and that this effect is not uniform across all problems.

the convergence of MOEA/D on a limited budget is affected by the choice of component-level parameters, and that the choice of parameters can have different impacts on different areas of the search space.

the choice of configuration is problem-specific, and that it may be necessary to consider a range of different configurations, and/or to adapt the configuration dynamically, to obtain good performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the convergence behaviour of decomposition-based optimisers over a limited budget is highly sensitive to the choice of component-level parameters, and that the sensitivity of convergence is different for different performance indicators.

the convergence of MOEA/D over a limited budget is affected by both the sharing and normalisation schemes, and that the effect of the normalisation scheme is not limited to the convergence in the vicinity of the reference point.

the convergence of MOEA/D on a limited budget is highly sensitive to choice of configuration parameters, and that the impact of configuration parameters on convergence may differ significantly from their impact on the long-run convergence of the algorithm.
